summary: RealityKit is an AR-first 3D simulation and rendering framework for Apple platforms, built around ARKit anchors, visionOS immersive spaces and Reality Composer Pro assets. BifrOSt is a 2D macOS-style desktop with no AR, spatial or 3D scene layer, so there is no counterpart to map.

features.note: The shell and apps are 2D retained views (springboard/sdk/src/view/); no scene graph.

features.apple: Scenes, Systems, Events (Scene management and logic)
features.note: No per-frame entity simulation API exists.

features.apple: Anchors, Views and attachments, Presentation UI
features.note: No AR tracking or camera-anchored content on BifrOSt.

features.apple: Collision detection, Simulations and motion, Physics joints and pins
features.note: No physics engine in the desktop stack.
The GPU presenter in springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs draws only 2D surfaces and glass; no 3D splat or compute-graph path.

gaps: No 3D scene or entity layer in the SDK
No AR or spatial anchoring; the platform does not target visionOS or ARKit-class hardware
